references.text: Matthew's account of the calling of the first disciples, including James and John, sons of Zebedee, who left everything and followed Jesus.
Mark's parallel account of the calling of Simon, Andrew, James, and John by the Sea of Galilee, where Jesus calls them to become fishers of men.
James and John, sons of Zebedee, are mentioned as part of the Twelve and given the nickname Boanerges.
James and John are listed among the twelve apostles chosen by Jesus.
The sons of Zebedee are present at another fishing scene where the disciples catch nothing without Jesus' intervention, parallel to the miraculous catch in Luke 5.
"Do not be afraid" – God's fundamental encouragement to His chosen ones, as God said to Abram. Jesus uses the same expression toward Simon.
"Do not be afraid, for I am with you" – God's word to Israel through Isaiah, reflected in Jesus' words to Simon about not fearing.
The Lord encourages Israel with the words "Do not be afraid," the same pattern Jesus follows when calling Simon to service.
Jeremiah describes fishermen whom God sends out to catch people – a prophetic background for Jesus' call to Simon to catch people.
Ezekiel's vision of fishermen standing along the water and catching fish in great numbers, an image pointing toward the great catch and the mission to catch people.
The parable of the net cast into the sea that catches all kinds of fish, a picture of God's kingdom gathering people, linked to the concept of catching people.
"Do not be afraid, you little flock" – Jesus again uses the expression "do not be afraid" toward the disciples, a recurring theme from the calling in Luke 5:10.
The Lord says to Paul: "Do not be afraid … for I have many people in this city" – the same pattern where Jesus encourages His servants not to fear but to gather people.
